issue.title: feat(rpc): make retry logic useable across clients
issue.body_html:
Part of #359

History: My original implementation of RPC retry logic was located in package:google_cloud_storage and meant for use in that package. @sigurdm needed equivalent functionality for package:google_cloud_pubsub so he moved it to a common location (package:google_cloud_rpc).

The intent of this PR is to make this RPC retry logic useable by all clients, hand-written and generated.

The broad strokes (does saying something like "broad strokes" make this seem more or less AI-written?):

  1. Remove the Google Cloud Storage-specific retry logic from package:google_cloud_rpc and replace it with the ability to retry errors based on either a predicate function or specific error codes.
  2. Changed the retry defaults to match Python (there is variation across implementations so I picked one)
  3. Changed the jittering logic to match the other languages' clients (the were all the same)
  4. Changed ServiceClient to accept a retry argument for every RPC method

The rest of the PR is clean-up in package:google_cloud_storage and package:google_cloud_pubsub to use the change functionality.

There are a few semi-related changes in package:google_cloud_storage (I noticed these because it does affect the retry strategy):

  • Changed deleteObjectAcl/patchObjectAcl to never be idempotent.
  • Changed deleteBucket to always be idempotent.
  • Changed uploadObjectFromSink to only consider the generation match when starting the transfer, not when retrying failed data chunk uploads.

One small semi-related change to package:google_cloud_pubsub:

  • Changed defaultRetry to match the service definition. @sigurdm could you check that I used the correct reference?

Question: Should every package export 'package:google_cloud_rpc/retry.dart'; so that developers don't have to explicitly depend on package:google_cloud_rpc if they want to modify their client's retry logic?

I talked to @natebosch and we will not be doing that.

## Code Review

This pull request refactors the retry mechanism across the Google Cloud Dart packages, introducing breaking changes to `ExponentialRetry` by removing built-in retryable errors in favor of explicit predicates or status codes, implementing full jitter, and dynamically determining idempotency within client methods rather than the retry runner. Additionally, it updates documentation, examples, and tests to align with these changes. A critical bug was identified in the newly added `isTransientError` helper in `pkgs/google_cloud_storage/lib/src/retry.dart`, where parsed REST-based `ServiceException` errors containing HTTP status codes in `status.code` would fail to be recognized as transient and thus would not be retried.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In REST-based APIs like Google Cloud Storage, the JSON error response is parsed into a `ServiceException` where `status.code` contains the HTTP status code (e.g., `503`), rather than a gRPC status code. Because `status?.code` is `503` (which is not in the gRPC status codes list `2 || 4 || 8 || 10 || 13 || 14` and is not `null`), the switch falls through to `_ => false`. This prevents transient REST errors with parsed JSON bodies from being retried. Adding the transient HTTP status codes to the first switch case resolves this issue.

```suggestion
    ServiceException(:final status, :final statusCode) =>
      switch (status?.code) {
        // gRPC status codes: UNKNOWN(2), DEADLINE_EXCEEDED(4),
        // RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED(8), ABORTED(10), INTERNAL(13), UNAVAILABLE(14).
        // HTTP status codes: 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
        2 || 4 || 8 || 10 || 13 || 14 ||
        408 || 429 || 500 || 502 || 503 || 504 => true,
        null =>
          statusCode == 408 ||
              statusCode == 429 ||
              statusCode == 500 ||
              statusCode == 502 ||
              statusCode == 503 ||
              statusCode == 504,
        _ => false,
      },
```
google_cloud_storage doesn't use gRPC so I removed all of these cases.
This seems unrelated to this PR.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `google.pubsub.v1` gRPC service configuration specifies a `backoffMultiplier` of `2` (or `1.3` in some versions), not `4`. A multiplier of `4` causes the retry delay to grow extremely fast, which deviates from the standard Pub/Sub retry policy. Please update this to `2` to match the service definition.

```suggestion
  delayMultiplier: 2,
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Update the test assertion to expect a `delayMultiplier` of `2` to align with the corrected default retry configuration.

```dart
      expect(defaultRetry.delayMultiplier, equals(2));
```

issue.title: [google_cloud_rpc] Wire RetryRunner and per-call RequestOptions into ServiceClient for generated REST clients
issue.body_html:
Context & Problem

PR #352 extracts RetryRunner, ExponentialRetry, NoDelayRetry, and defaultIsRetryable into package:google_cloud_rpc/retry.dart (keep: list) so google_cloud_storage and google_cloud_pubsub (#353) can share a common retry implementation (#346).

However, three transport and codegen gaps remain before RetryRunner can reliably protect all 20+ generated REST client packages in generated/*:

  1. ServiceClient._makeRequest() Does Not Invoke RetryRunner or Accept RequestOptions:

    • ServiceClient._makeRequest() in generated/google_cloud_rpc/lib/service_client.dart still executes raw http.Client.send calls without invoking RetryRunner, and provides no mechanism for callers to configure client-level retry policies, per-call timeouts, or custom headers (RequestOptions).
    • By contrast, sibling sidekick-generated SDKs (google-cloud-rust and google-cloud-swift) wrap every generated client transport in a RetryLoop consulting a client-level RetryPolicy and per-call RequestOptions.

  2. Bug: ServiceException.fromHttpResponse Throws FormatException on HTML 502/503/504 Responses (Bypassing RetryRunner):

    • In generated/google_cloud_rpc/lib/src/exceptions.dart:60, ServiceException.fromHttpResponse(http.Response response, String body) calls JsonDecode(body) whenever body.isNotEmpty without catching FormatException.
    • When a Google Front End (GFE) or load balancer returns a transient 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, or 504 Gateway Timeout with an HTML error page (<html>...), JsonDecode(body) throws an uncaught FormatException before ServiceException is constructed.
    • Because defaultIsRetryable in retry.dart (#352) checks if (error is ServiceException) (500, 502, 503, 504, 408, 429), an uncaught FormatException completely bypasses RetryRunner on gateway errors.
3. **AIP-4222 `x-goog-request-params` Routing Headers & AIP-155 Auto-Populated `request_id` UUIDv4 (`sidekick/dart`)**: - `sidekick/api` (`routing_info.go`) already parses `google.api.routing` annotations into `api.Method.Routing` and `auto_populated_fields` (`request_id` UUIDv4) into `api.Method.AutoPopulated`, and `sidekick/rust` emits both, whereas `sidekick/dart` currently drops them. - Emitting `x-goog-request-params` is required by [AIP-4222](https://google.aip.dev/client-libraries/4222) for regional/tenant routing, and auto-populating empty `request_id` fields with a UUIDv4 ([AIP-155](https://google.aip.dev/155) / [AIP-4235](https://google.aip.dev/client-libraries/4235)) makes mutating `POST` RPCs idempotent so `RetryRunner` can safely retry them on transient failures.

Proposed Solution

  1. Harden ServiceException.fromHttpResponse and Extend ServiceClient in package:google_cloud_rpc:
    • Wrap JsonDecode(body) in ServiceException.fromHttpResponse (exceptions.dart:60) in a try / on FormatException block that falls back to constructing the status-code-mapped ServiceException with response.reasonPhrase ?? body when the error payload is non-JSON/HTML.
    • Add an optional RetryRunner retry parameter to ServiceClient({...}) (defaulting to const NoDelayRetry() or per-service defaults passed by generated clients).
    • Add a RequestOptions class in package:google_cloud_rpc supporting per-call Duration? timeout, RetryRunner? retry, and Map<String, String>? headers.
    • Update ServiceClient._makeRequest() to execute requests through (options?.retry ?? this.retry).run(...) with optional timeout enforcement.
  2. Update sidekick/dart Generator Templates (googleapis/librarian):
    • Pass service-specific retry defaults (from service config / librarian.yaml) when constructing ServiceClient.
    • Add an optional RequestOptions? options parameter to generated RPC methods in method.mustache.
    • Emit x-goog-request-params headers from api.Method.Routing (AIP-4222) and auto-populate unset request_id fields (api.Method.AutoPopulated) with a UUIDv4 before entering RetryRunner.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ServiceException.fromHttpResponse gracefully handles non-JSON/HTML 502/503/504 error bodies without throwing FormatException, allowing RetryRunner to retry gateway errors.
  • ServiceClient in package:google_cloud_rpc supports RetryRunner and per-request RequestOptions.
  • Generated REST clients in generated/* support configurable retry policies, per-call RequestOptions, x-goog-request-params routing headers, and auto-populated request_id UUIDs.

issue.body_html:
Adds AckSettings and background batching and retry for
Subscription.acknowledge and Subscription.modifyAckDeadline.

  • Subscription.acknowledge(ReceivedMessage) and
    Subscription.modifyAckDeadline(ReceivedMessage, int) now buffer
    requests and flush them in batches according to
    AckSettings.batching, deduplicating ack IDs (and grouping by the
    latest deadline per ack ID) and retrying transient failures using
    AckSettings.retry.
  • Subscription validates ackSettings.batching on construction
    against the 512,000-byte server limit for Acknowledge and
    ModifyAckDeadline requests.
  • Added Subscription.close() and Subscription.isClosed to flush
    buffered acknowledgments and deadline modifications and await
    in-flight batches before shutdown.
  • Subscription.modifyAckDeadline, Subscription.modifyAckDeadlineNow,
    PubSub.modifyAckDeadline, and ReceivedMessage.modifyAckDeadline
    validate that ackDeadlineSeconds is between 0 and 600 seconds;
    PubSub.pull validates maxMessages > 0 and PubSub.streamingPull
    validates streamAckDeadlineSeconds synchronously.
  • Message now always copies data (Uint8List.fromList) and wraps
    attributes in Map.unmodifiable.
  • Added ReceivedMessage.deliveryAttempt and toString() on Message
    and ReceivedMessage, and made ReceivedMessage.acknowledge and
    ReceivedMessage.modifyAckDeadline throw StateError when no
    handler is configured.

Part 4 of 5 (followed by #339).

issue.title: feat(pubsub): add resilient parallel streaming pull
issue.body_html:
Adds resilient parallel streaming pull to Subscription.streamingPull
and routes batched acknowledgments and deadline modifications over
active streams when available.

  • Subscription.streamingPull opens maxConcurrentStreams parallel
    StreamingPull connections and multiplexes their messages onto a
    single returned Stream<ReceivedMessage>.
  • Reconnects automatically with exponential backoff (RetryRunner) when
    a stream fails with a retryable error or closes unexpectedly, and
    resets the retry state once a stream receives a message or remains
    connected for at least 15 seconds.
  • When maxConcurrentStreams > 1, an individual stream exhausting its
    retries does not terminate the combined stream while sibling streams
    remain active.
  • Batched acknowledgments and deadline modifications from
    Subscription.acknowledge, Subscription.modifyAckDeadline,
    ReceivedMessage.acknowledge, and
    ReceivedMessage.modifyAckDeadline are written to an active
    StreamingPull request stream when one is open, falling back to
    unary RPCs with retry when no stream is active.
  • Propagates pause and resume across all active underlying streams,
    and in Subscription.close() cancels active streaming pulls before
    flushing pending batches via unary RPCs.
  • Adds PubSub.streamingPullWithStream for bidirectional
    request/response stream management.

Stacked on #292.
